title: Senior DevOps Engineer
description:
Role Overview The role reports into the UK and involves regular collaboration with UK-based stakeholders and teams across OCU Digital. 
 The Senior DevOps Engineer is responsible for the design, governance and continuous improvement of DevOps and application reliability across OCU Digital, ensuring digital platforms are built, secured, deployed and operated efficiently, consistently and resiliently across all environments. 
 Working across OCU One, Data and Dynamics, the role sets and governs standards for CI/CD, build and release security, deployment automation, runtime configuration, observability and Site Reliability Engineering (SRE), bridging Engineering, Cloud & Infrastructure, Security and Architecture. 
 Key Responsibilities 
 1. DevOps Tooling, Boards & Governance Own and govern the DevOps tooling landscape, with explicit accountability for Azure DevOps configuration and administration. Define and govern Azure DevOps Boards work item types, process templates and lifecycle models (e.g. Requirements, Change Requests, Work Requests, Bugs and Tasks). Own state models, mandatory fields, validation rules and workflow controls to ensure consistency, auditability and traceability. Ensure consistent usage of DevOps Boards across Digital platforms to support change control, compliance and reporting requirements. Maintain end-to-end traceability from demand intake through delivery, deployment and release. 
 2. DevOps & CI/CD Standards and Governance Define, own and continuously evolve CI/CD standards, templates and reusable pipeline patterns. Govern how build, test, security scanning, deployment and rollback stages are implemented across platforms. Enforce secure build and release practices aligned with security and architecture standards. Own the operation of CI/CD pipelines, ensuring reliability, performance and rapid recovery from failure. Provide clear guidance and decision-making on CI/CD tooling, patterns and usage. 
 3. Deployment, Environment & Release Management Define standardised deployment and release models, including automated releases and rollback mechanisms. Manage environment strategies across development, test, QA and production environments. Govern access control and environment permissions in collaboration with Cloud & Infrastructure and Security. Ensure release processes are auditable, predictable and aligned to risk and change controls. Support platform teams during complex or high-risk releases. 
 4. Site Reliability Engineering (SRE) & Performance Systems Design and govern the application-layer SRE monitoring and performance management system. Define and manage service reliability standards including SLIs, SLOs and error budgets. Build and standardise monitoring and observability dashboards covering availability, latency, errors and saturation. Lead reliability activities such as fault injection, resilience testing and reliability drills. Proactively identify reliability risks and drive preventative engineering improvements. 
 5. Observability, Incident Management & Operational Excellence Own the observability strategy, ensuring consistent use of metrics, logs and traces across platforms. Resolve major platform and application incidents, acting as incident commander when required. Ensure runbooks, handover packages and operational documentation are prepared and maintained. Lead post-incident reviews and ensure corrective actions are delivered and tracked. Improve operational maturity through standardised documentation, runbooks and operational tooling. 
 Key Skills & Experience 
 Essential Skills Extensive hands-on experience in DevOps and SRE practices in complex, multi-platform environments. Strong expertise in CI/CD tooling including Azure DevOps and GitHub Actions. Proven experience defining CI/CD standards, templates and secure build pipelines. Deep understanding of cloud-native architectures, Kubernetes and application runtime configuration. Strong background in SRE concepts including SLIs, SLOs, error budgets and reliability governance. Experience designing monitoring, observability and performance management systems. Proven ability to lead and resolve high-severity platform incidents. Strong stakeholder management and cross-functional working. Experience producing high-quality technical documentation and runbooks. 
 Desirable Skills Experience operating DevOps and SRE across custom applications, data platforms and SaaS environments. Familiarity with ISO27001, SOC2 or similar enterprise governance frameworks. Experience implementing DevSecOps controls and secure supply-chain practices. Experience running resilience testing, chaos engineering or fault injection exercises. Knowledge of Azure Fabric, Databricks or modern data platforms. Experience supporting business-critical or safety-sensitive systems. Track record of building and scaling DevOps capabilities in growing organisations.

title: Senior DevOps / Site Reliability Engineer (SMTS)
description:
Role Type On-site - Permanent - Full-time - Associate Description We are looking for a Senior Member of Technical Staff (SMTS) in DevOps to build and run the infrastructure behind our energy and IoT platform. The SMTS will own AWS and Kubernetes in production, keep services reliable, and make sure we get maximum value from every rupee of cloud spend. This is a hands-on senior individual contributor role. It requires strong DevOps and AWS capability, deep Docker and Kubernetes experience in production, a proven record of cloud cost optimisation, and site reliability practice covering SLOs, observability and incident response. Strong programming skills in at least one language such as Python, Go or Java are essential, because automation here is built as software. This is an AI-native engineering environment: AI coding agents such as Claude Code and Cursor are part of the daily workflow. The role requires 5+ years of relevant experience. THE WORK Key Responsibilities AWS Infrastructure Design, build and operate AWS infrastructure across compute, networking, storage, managed databases and IAM, with ownership of resilience and security posture. Write and maintain infrastructure as code with Terraform or equivalent, using review, testing and versioning like any other software. Manage networking, VPC design, DNS, load balancing and access control across environments. Partner with security on secrets management, patching, vulnerability scanning and least-privilege access. Docker Kubernetes Own Kubernetes clusters in production, including upgrades, autoscaling, resource management, networking and multi-environment setup. Define container standards with Docker: lean images, secure base images and consistent build practices. Package and deploy services with Helm or equivalent, and drive GitOps practices where they help. Troubleshoot workloads across pods, nodes, networking and storage. Cost Optimisation Own AWS and Kubernetes cost visibility, with tagging, dashboards and per-service cost attribution. Reduce spend through rightsizing, autoscaling, Spot and Graviton usage, Savings Plans, storage lifecycle policies and removal of idle resources. Review architecture and capacity decisions for cost impact before they reach production. Report cost trends and savings to engineering leadership with clear recommendations. Site Reliability Define and track SLIs and SLOs for critical services, and use them to guide reliability work. Build monitoring, logging, tracing and alerting that is actionable rather than noisy. Lead incident response, run blameless post-mortems and drive fixes for recurring causes. Plan capacity and run load and failure testing before peak demand or major releases. Write runbooks and automate repetitive operational work so on-call stays sustainable. CI/CD Automation Design and maintain CI/CD pipelines with automated testing, safe rollouts and fast rollback. Write production-quality automation and internal tooling in Python, Go or Java rather than relying on ad hoc scripts. Mentor engineers on deployment, observability and production ownership. Use Claude Code, Cursor and equivalent AI coding agents for infrastructure code, automation and log analysis, and review AI-assisted changes carefully. THE ENVIRONMENT Technology Environment Cloud: AWS (EC2, EKS, VPC, RDS, S3, IAM, CloudWatch). Containers Orchestration: Docker, Kubernetes and Helm. Infrastructure as Code: Terraform or equivalent. CI/CD GitOps: GitHub Actions, Jenkins and Argo CD. Observability: Prometheus, Grafana, OpenTelemetry, Loki and Sentry. Cost Management: AWS Cost Explorer, Kubecost or equivalent. Programming: Python, Go, Java and Bash. Services Supported: Java, Spring Boot, Python, Django, FastAPI and Node.js. Data Messaging: PostgreSQL, Redis, Kafka, MQTT and Apache Flink. AI Tooling: Claude Code and Cursor. WHAT WE RE LOOKING FOR Qualifications Experience Essential: DevOps AWS 5+ years of experience in DevOps, platform or site reliability engineering for production systems. Strong hands-on AWS experience across compute, networking, storage, managed databases and IAM. Infrastructure as code (Terraform or equivalent) and CI/CD pipelines built and maintained first-hand. Strong Linux and networking fundamentals. Essential: Docker Kubernetes Deep hands-on Kubernetes experience in production, including cluster-level ownership rather than only deploying to it. Strong Docker and container fundamentals, including image security and build optimisation. Essential: Cost Optimisation Site Reliability Demonstrated cloud cost reduction with measurable savings. Experience defining SLOs, building monitoring and alerting, and participating in on-call. Incident response and post-mortem experience on customer-impacting issues. Strong debugging across application, container, network and infrastructure layers. Essential: Programming Strong coding ability in at least one language such as Python, Go or Java, writing maintainable automation and tooling rather than only shell scripts. Essential: Ways of Working Ability to work independently and bring clarity to ambiguous operational problems. Clear written communication across runbooks, post-mortems and design documents. Bias towards fixing causes rather than symptoms, and automating rather than repeating. Fluent use of Claude Code, Cursor or equivalent AI development tools in daily engineering work. Desirable AWS Certified Solutions Architect, DevOps Engineer or CKA certification. GitOps with Argo CD or Flux. Operating Kafka, Flink or time-series databases in production. Chaos engineering or disaster recovery planning. Security and compliance practices such as ISO 27001 or SOC 2. IoT, energy, industrial or real-time data platforms

title: Senior Principal - Platform Engineer LAN
description:
Job Purpose The Principal Engineer builds and runs GSKs local area network and campus switching platform as automated, secure, self-service infrastructure, sets the engineering standard within that platform, mentors the engineers around them, and treats the teams who consume the platform as customers. The role works through infrastructure-as-code and golden paths rather than manual configuration, uses AI-assisted engineering across code generation, review and testing, and engineers reliability in by defining SLOs, instrumenting for observability and automating away toil. This is the senior hands-on engineering role in the platform team, working across local area network and campus switching to integrate and assure delivery as well as building. Engineering roadmap and direction sit with the Engineering Director, reference architecture and standards sit with the Platform Architect, backlog order sits with the Product Owner, and deep reliability engineering sits with the Site Reliability Engineer deployed from Reliability Engineering Operations. Key Responsibilities Design, build and automate platform infrastructure using infrastructure-as-code and golden paths, so that provisioning is repeatable rather than reconstructed each time. Use AI-assisted engineering across code generation, review and testing to accelerate delivery and raise quality, reviewing AI-generated output before it is merged. Build self-service capabilities and paved roads that reduce friction for consuming teams, so adoption does not depend on the platform teams availability. Engineer for reliability by defining SLOs, instrumenting platforms for observability and automating to reduce toil, working with the Site Reliability Engineer on standards. Set and uphold engineering standards, secure-by-default practices and code quality within the platform, and hold them in code review. Contribute to incident response and drive permanent automated fixes with Reliability Engineering rather than repeating manual recovery. Mentor and technically lead other engineers, including partner engineers, linking engineering work to platform OKRs and outcomes. Integrate and assure supplier or managed-service components, holding partner-delivered engineering to the same standards and code quality as internal work. Work the platforms manual task and toil backlog, converting identified candidates into automation and evidencing the effort removed. Close observability coverage gaps for the platform, so that reliability can be measured rather than inferred. Contribute engineering-led items to the platform backlog held by the Product Owner, including technical debt, upgrade and automation work, with the cost of not doing them stated. Apply the reference architectures and patterns set by the Platform Architect, and raise a case for change rather than diverging locally. Key Relationships/Customers Business Stakeholders Internal GSK teams consuming the platform as customers of its self-service capability Quality and compliance functions where the platform supports GxP activity Tech Stakeholders Engineering Director as line manager and owner of the engineering roadmap Platform Architect for reference architectures, patterns and standards Product Owner for backlog order and acceptance of engineering-led items Site Reliability Engineer and Reliability Engineering Operations for SLOs, observability and incident prevention Other Principal Engineers and platform engineers across the domain Other Managed service partners contributing engineering capacity to the platform. Technology vendors during evaluation and proof of concept Professional Qualifications Degree in a technology or engineering discipline, or equivalent practical experience (e.g., Computer Science, Software Engineering, Electronics). Relevant technical certifications desirable (e.g., a recognised cloud certification for AWS, GCP or Azure, Certified Kubernetes Administrator, or a network vendor certification relevant to the platform). Area of Specialisation Hands-on platform engineering in cloud, network or digital workplace, covering infrastructure-as-code, CI/CD and containers where relevant. Automation-first and secure-by-default engineering, with an SRE mindset covering SLOs, observability and toil reduction. Why is this level of Education Required Deep engineering credentials are needed because the role sets the engineering standard other engineers and partner teams build to, and that standard has to hold under code review rather than by assertion. Experience Required Overall 15 years typically 6-8 years in platform, infrastructure or software engineering, including at least two years as the senior technical voice in a team. Deep hands-on depth in the relevant platform domain, whether cloud and hosting, network or digital workplace. Practical experience of infrastructure-as-code, for example Terraform, applied to production estates rather than proofs of concept. Experience with CI/CD pipelines, and with containers and Kubernetes where relevant to the platform. Track record building self-service capability that other teams adopted without hand-holding. Experience instrumenting for observability, defining SLOs and reducing toil through automation. Experience with AI-assisted engineering tooling, including judgement about when generated output is not fit to merge. Extensive experience engineering enterprise local area networks and campus switching services. Strong knowledge of routing, switching, segmentation, resilience and complex fault diagnosis. Evidence of applying standards and automation to improve deployment quality, reliability or supportability. Desirable Requirements Professional level enterprise networking certification, such as CCNP Enterprise or JNCIP Enterprise Routing and Switching. Experience with application programming interfaces, infrastructure as code or network assurance platforms. Experience supporting manufacturing, laboratory or operational technology networks. Skills/Background Automation-first instinct, treating a repeated manual task as a defect rather than as work. Code review discipline, holding quality without becoming a bottleneck. Mentoring ability with engineers of varying experience, including partner engineers outside the line. Judgement about when AI-generated code is fit to merge and when it is not. Customer mindset toward consuming teams, who can route around a platform that is hard to use. Willingness to make technical debt and its cost visible rather than absorbing it silently. title: Senior Staff Engineer, Kubernetes Platform & Networking
description:
Who are we Equinix is the worlds digital infrastructure company, shortening the path to connectivity to enable the innovations that enrich our work, life and planet.
 A place where bold ideas are welcomed, human connection is valued, and everyone has the opportunity to shape their future. Help us challenge assumptions, uncover bias, and remove barriersbecause progress starts with fresh ideas. Youll find belonging, purpose, and a team that welcomes youbecause when you feel valued, youre empowered to do your best work. Job Summary We are looking for a Senior Staff Engineer to join the Reliability Engineering team that operates a bare-metal Kubernetes platform across multiple metro locations. The platform''s architecture is defined and the build is underway, you will help deploy, operate and continuously improve it, from OS provisioning on racked servers through a multi-cluster fleet managed from a central management plane, with a software-defined data plane deployed via GitOps. This is a deliberately broad role. We are not looking for someone who owns a layer and hands everything below it across a boundary. You will work alongside the teams that own the physical hardware, the underlay network, and the data plane software, and you need enough fluency in all three to reason about a fault before escalating it. Where you find the design falls short in practice, we expect you to say so and to shape how it evolves. You will join the Digital Interconnection Engineering organization. The team owns the full application stack for interconnection and the Kubernetes platform for the software-defined data plane across multiple metros. We operate with an automation-first, GitOps-driven culture and a strong commitment to operational rigor, documented runbooks, and blameless postmortems. Responsibilities OS Provisioning Bare-Metal Infrastructure Own OS installation (Debian/Ubuntu) across bare-metal servers in multiple metros using PXE/iPXE imaging and cloud-init, and harden the OS prior to cluster bootstrap Build and maintain a repeatable, zero-touch provisioning pipeline so every metro is deployed consistently without manual per-node intervention Partner with the teams that own the hardware on BIOS/firmware baselines, high-speed NIC configuration and disk layout standards (separate NVMe for etcd, SSD for OS) and be able to diagnose faults at that layer, not just report them Kubernetes Control Plane Worker Nodes Deploy and operate Kubernetes clusters across all metros with quorum-based control-plane fault tolerance and correct failure-domain placement across racks, PDUs, or availability zones Maintain the Layer 4 load balancer or keepalived VIP fronting all kube-apiserver instances, so no client depends on a single node Manage worker node provisioning, CNI configuration, and end-to-end cluster validation before workloads are onboarded CI/CD Data Plane Deployment Build and own the CI/CD pipeline that deploys the software-defined data plane, including automated throughput and latency validation gates that must pass before promotion to production. The data plane software itself is configured and troubleshot by the team that owns it, your ownership is the pipeline and the gates Own data-plane observability: monitoring, alerting thresholds, and operational runbooks Network Operate on top of a multi-metro underlay and partner with network and security teams on VLANs, BGP peering, NIC bonding, private connectivity, firewall rules and segmentation Validate connectivity end to end across environments, and troubleshoot far enough into the network layer to isolate a problem before handing it over OS Kubernetes Upgrades Plan and execute rolling OS and Kubernetes upgrades across the fleet with zero unplanned downtime; maintain tested upgrade runbooks and validated etcd snapshot/restore procedures before every major change Own the etcd snapshot schedule, retention policy, and offsite storage; verify restore runbooks before each site goes live Apply the platform''s patching cadence across the fleet, tracking CVEs affecting the OS, Kubernetes and cluster components Management Plane Administer the centralized management plane across all clusters, including RBAC, cluster registration and policy enforcement, and keep production and non-production management planes strictly isolated to prevent blast-radius cascades from configuration changes Drive GitOps-based fleet configuration management to keep clusters consistent, auditable, and drift-free On-Call Incident Management Own your shift of a follow-the-sun on-call rotation, and lead incident response for control-plane, data-plane, and network events Drive blameless postmortems and systematically eliminate recurring failure modes through automation, better runbooks, and sharper alerting Contribute to the shared incident-command process, and maintain the runbooks for the systems you operate What Success Looks Like, First 9-12 Months Provisioning is fully automated and repeatable, new nodes and metros brought up with no manual per-node steps Deployment pipeline in production, with throughput and latency gates enforced before promotion Management plane administered across all clusters; production and non-production planes isolated; GitOps driving cluster configuration OS and Kubernetes upgrades executed on cadence across the fleet with documented, tested runbooks etcd snapshot and restore tested and signed off before each site goes live Observability and alerting in place for the systems you operate, including the data plane Recurring failure modes measurably reduced through automation and runbook improvements Qualifications Required OS bare metal: Deep hands-on Linux/Ubuntu provisioning at scale, PXE/iPXE imaging, cloud-init, BIOS/firmware management, OS hardening Hardware fluency: Comfortable with BMC/IPMI, SMART data and platform sensors; able to diagnose disk, memory, NIC and power faults and work with vendors through warranty replacement Kubernetes: Strong experience deploying and operating RKE2 or kubeadm clusters on bare metal, etcd operations, kube-apiserver HA, CNI (Multus/SR-IOV), multi-cluster fleet management Rancher or equivalent management plane: Production experience managing multiple clusters through Rancher Prime, Rancher, or comparable fleet tooling CI/CD for infrastructure: GitOps or pipeline-driven infrastructure deployment, Ansible, Terraform, ArgoCD, or Fleet Networking: Hands-on with VLANs, BGP, bonded NICs, SR-IOV and private connectivity, with enough depth to troubleshoot across the boundary rather than only consume it Upgrades: Demonstrated zero-downtime rolling upgrades of both OS and Kubernetes across a multi-node fleet Operational rigor: Experience running platforms where availability is measured in minutes of downtime per year, and where an unreviewed change is the most likely cause of an outage On-call: Comfortable owning an on-call shift and leading infrastructure incident response Automation mindset: Everything-as-code, repeatable and auditable; strong bias toward automation over manual operations Preferred Familiarity with 6WIND VSR or other DPDK-based data planes, enough to build and validate a deployment and performance-testing pipeline around one SR-IOV NIC tuning and data-plane performance validation SDN or private-connectivity platforms (Equinix Fabric, VyOS, or equivalent) Familiarity with LLM provider APIs and AI/agent gateway proxying patterns, since inference traffic from multiple providers transits this platform Experience operating infrastructure across geographically distributed sites Equinix is committed to ensuring that our employment process is open to all individuals, including those with a disability.If you are a qualified candidate and need assistance or an accommodation, please let us know by completing this form. description:
Job Summary 
 Job Title. - Site Reliability Engineer (SRE) Department - Employee Services Technology Operations - CIO RUN Function Experience Level - 4 - 8 Years Location - Pune, India (Hybrid) Shift Pattern - APAC and EMEA Shift Reporting Manager - Yashwant Sinha 

 Role Overview 
 We are seeking an experienced Site Reliability Engineer (SRE) with 4 to 8 years of technical expertise to join our SRE and observability team within the CIO RUN function. In this role, you will act as a critical bridge between engineering and operations, driving system stability, proactive detection, and rapid incident mitigation across enterprise systems. You will be responsible for hands-on configuration of observability platforms, triaging system alerts and user reports, managing incident response workflows, and enforcing end-to-end ITIL lifecycles (Incident, Problem, and Change Management). 

 Key Responsibilities 
 Partner and collaborate with end users to understand administrative needs, resolve issues and meet business requirements. Handle both end user tickets and monitoring tickets from ITIL perspective with end to end ownership maintaining required response and resolution SLA targets. Liaise with the problem manager to identify repeated incidents and engage with level 2 or domain teams for permanent fixes. Able to manage high impact major incidents P1/P2 and able to perform initial level troubleshooting and triaging. Develop and mentor others around application customization via custom objects, validation rules, workflows, flows, process builder, etc Implement, own and optimize internal processes to improve efficiency. Document procedures, policies, and systems in Runbooks, SOPs and KEDBs/KB Articles. Manage and own system administration and help streamline business functionality including: profiles/permissions, role hierarchy, security models, application customization, reports and dashboards, etc 

 Proactive Monitoring Observability 
 Perform hands-on configuration and tuning of synthetic monitors, application performance monitoring (APM), dashboards, and alert rules in platforms such as Datadog and Dynatrace. Drive continuous reduction of alert noise and fatigue by establishing alert correlation rules and actionable threshold triggers. Assist in application onboarding to ensure proper logging, tracing, and metric standards are enforced prior to operational go-live. 

 Triage Incident Management 
 Actively triage incoming system alerts and user-reported issues, minimizing Mean Time to Detect (MTTD) and Mean Time to Restore (MTTR). Participate in incident swarming and real-time operational response utilizing modern collaboration and ITSM tools such as Incident.io, Datadog, Jira, and Slack. Oversee the lifecycle of monitoring tickets, maintaining strict adherence to SLA compliance and response metrics. 

 Problem Change Management 
 Conduct thorough Root Cause Analysis (RCA) and facilitate Post-Incident Reviews (PIR) to eliminate recurring incidents. Maintain and expand the Known Error Database (KEDB) and runbook documentation to mitigate Single Point of Failure (SPOF) risks across operational workflows. Review and govern change requests, verifying risk assessments and rollback plans to maintain operational continuity. 

 Tooling Integration Management 
 Monitor, troubleshoot, and support bi-directional SaaS integrations and data pipelines (e.g., Salesforce-to-Zuora, Workato, AWS Lambda, and EHC/Zendesk platforms). Ensure seamless data flow across ticketing and incident management ecosystems, collaborating with engineering leads to resolve integration breaks. 

 Required Qualifications 
 Experience: 4 to 8 years of experience in Site Reliability Engineering (SRE), IT Operations, System Engineering, or NOC environments. Observability Mastery: Hands-on experience configuring observability stacks, including log aggregation, metric creation, APM tracing, and visual dashboards using tools like Datadog, Dynatrace, or New Relic. ITIL Proficiency: Strong working knowledge of ITIL frameworks, specifically Incident, Problem, and Change Management integration. Cloud Architecture: Technical experience with cloud platforms (AWS/GCP), API integrations, payload troubleshooting, and database querying via SQL. Scripting Automation: Familiarity with scripting languages (Python, Go, PowerShell, or Bash) for automating tasks, processing telemetry data, or building operational reports. Operational Drive: Proven track record in reducing alert fatigue, managing complex system environments, and maintaining composure during high-priority outage events. 

 Nice to Have 
 ITIL 4 Foundation certification or specialized certifications in Incident/Problem Management. Prior experience in service-based or consulting environments with broad, multi-client operational exposure. Background in a global technology company supporting enterprise-grade, business-critical SaaS systems and distributed topologies. Hybrid: In this role, our hybrid experience is designed at the team level to give you a rich onsite experience packed with connection, collaboration, learning, and celebration - while also giving you flexibility to work remotely for part of the week. This role must attend our local office for part of the week. The specific in-office schedule is to be determined by the hiring manager.

title: Sr Principal - Cloud Platform Engineer - Cloud Native
description:
Job Summary 
 The Principal Cloud Platform Engineer - Cloud Native builds and runs automation scripts and tools (IaC / Terraform) to streamline provisioning, configuration, and management of Cloud PaaS and Serverless Services, and sets the engineering standard within those services, mentors the engineers around them, and treats the teams who consume the platform as customers. The role works through infrastructure-as-code and golden paths rather than manual configuration, uses AI-assisted engineering across code generation, review and testing, and engineers reliability in by defining SLOs, instrumenting for observability and automating away toil. This is the senior hands-on engineering role in the platform team, insourced at the grades covered by this description while engineering at G7b and below is delivered through managed service partners, so the role integrates and assures partner components as well as building. Engineering roadmap and direction sit with the Engineering Director, reference architecture and standards sit with the Platform Architect, backlog order sits with the Product Owner, and deep reliability engineering sits with the Site Reliability Engineer deployed from Reliability Engineering Operations. 
 
 Key Responsibilities 
 Design, build and automate platform infrastructure using infrastructure-as-code and golden paths, so that provisioning is repeatable rather than reconstructed each time. Use AI-assisted engineering across code generation, review and testing to accelerate delivery and raise quality, reviewing AI-generated output before it is merged. Build self-service capabilities and paved roads that reduce friction for consuming teams, so adoption does not depend on the platform teams availability. Engineer for reliability by defining SLOs, instrumenting platforms for observability and automating to reduce toil, working with the Site Reliability Engineer on standards. Set and uphold engineering standards, secure-by-default practices and code quality within the platform, and hold them in code review. Contribute to incident response and drive permanent automated fixes with Reliability Engineering rather than repeating manual recovery. Mentor and technically lead other engineers, including partner engineers, linking engineering work to platform OKRs and outcomes. Integrate and assure supplier or managed-service components, holding partner-delivered engineering to the same standards and code quality as internal work. Work the platforms manual task and toil backlog, converting identified candidates into automation and evidencing the effort removed. Close observability coverage gaps for the platform, so that reliability can be measured rather than inferred. Contribute engineering-led items to the platform backlog held by the Product Owner, including technical debt, upgrade and automation work, with the cost of not doing them stated. Apply the reference architectures and patterns set by the Platform Architect, and raise a case for change rather than diverging locally. 
 
 Educational Background 
 Degree in a technology or engineering discipline, or equivalent practical experience (e.g., Computer Science, Software Engineering, Electronics). Relevant technical certifications desirable (e.g., a recognised cloud certification for AWS, GCP or Azure, Certified Kubernetes Administrator, or a network vendor certification relevant to the platform). 
 
 Area of Specialisation 
 Hands-on platform engineering in cloud, network or digital workplace, covering infrastructure-as-code, CI/CD and containers where relevant. Automation-first and secure-by-default engineering, with an SRE mindset covering SLOs, observability and toil reduction. 
 
 Experience Required 
 Typically 6-8 years in cloud, infrastructure or software engineering, including at least two years as the senior technical voice in a team. Deep hands-on depth in Cloud PaaS and Serverless Technologies across Azure, Azure Local and GCP Proficient in writing scripts using Terraform, Python, Ansible, Json and PowerShell Experience with building, configuring and managing Cloud AI Services (e.g. Azure OpenAI, AI Search, Azure Machine Learning, Google Document AI, BigQuery AI) Practical experience of infrastructure-as-code, for example Terraform, applied to production estates rather than proofs of concept. Strong expertise in Azure/GCP application services (e.g. Logic Apps, Function Apps, App Services, cloud run, pub/sub) for designing and implementing scalable, secure, and cloud-native solutions. Experience with CI/CD pipelines, and with containers and Kubernetes where relevant to the platform. Track record building self-service capability that other teams adopted without hand-holding. Experience instrumenting for observability, defining SLOs and reducing toil through automation. Experience with AI-assisted engineering tooling, including judgement about when generated output is not fit to merge. 
 
 Desirable 
 Proficient in building solutions using container services - AKS GKE Hands-on experience deploying container solutions, including Docker containers, and managing K8s deployments using YAML and Helm charts Familiarity with multi-cloud deployments using cloud tools like Camunda, GitHub Action, Azure Arc, Google Anthos etc. Knowledge of Pharma practices, GxP, Validation, Audit readiness and how to optimize delivery to accommodate these critical practices 
 
 Skills/Background 
 Automation-first instinct, treating a repeated manual task as a defect rather than as work. Code review discipline, holding quality without becoming a bottleneck. Mentoring ability with engineers of varying experience, including partner engineers outside the line. Judgement about when AI-generated code is fit to merge and when it is not. Customer mindset toward consuming teams, who can route around a platform that is hard to use. Willingness to make technical debt and its cost visible rather than absorbing it silently. 
 
 Skills 
 Terraform Python Ansible Kubernetes Docker Azure GCP CI/CD Observability

title: Sr Principal - P&C Platform Engineer
description:
Job Summary 
 Build, automate and run the platform that 50,000+ employees across [X] countries use to communicate and collaborate - Microsoft Teams, SharePoint Online and OneDrive, Exchange Online, the Microsoft 365 apps, Power Platform and Microsoft 365 Copilot. This is the hands-on build role. The Platform Engineer takes architecture direction and a prioritised backlog and turns them into working, tested, automated, documented configuration in production. The expectation is engineering rather than administration: configuration expressed as code and deployed through pipelines, not clicked through a portal and remembered by whoever was on shift. The role also runs what it builds. Platform Engineers own the operational health of their workloads - diagnosing the awkward, intermittent, only-happens-in-Tokyo problems that never reproduce in a lab, and eliminating the root cause rather than closing the ticket. 
 
 Responsibilities 
 Design, build, test and deploy configuration across the Microsoft 365 estate: Teams policies, SharePoint and OneDrive settings, Exchange Online transport and mail flow, Purview policies, Entra ID groups and Conditional Access as it applies to collaboration workloads. Implement to the reference architecture and standards set by the Principal Architect; raise a design challenge when reality does not match the design rather than quietly deviating. Deliver backlog items from sprint to production with the tests, telemetry, documentation and rollback path included - done means running and observable, not merely configured. Build and maintain integrations using Microsoft Graph and platform APIs; write the connective tissue between M365, ServiceNow, HR systems and the wider application estate. Automate everything that would otherwise be done twice. Provisioning, lifecycle, reporting, remediation, joiner/mover/leaver flows, licence assignment and reclamation. Express tenant configuration as code in version control; build and maintain CI/CD pipelines for policy and solution deployment with automated validation and staged ring-based rollout. Replace manual runbook steps with self-healing and self-service; treat a recurring manual task as a defect with a backlog item attached. Own operational health of assigned workloads: monitoring, alerting, capacity, service health response and performance. Investigate and resolve complex incidents and problems - third-line escalation for collaboration platform issues - and drive permanent root-cause elimination. Participate in an on-call rotation for major incidents affecting the collaboration platform. Manage the continuous change stream from Microsoft: assess message centre and roadmap items, test in a lab tenant, and implement, defer or disable with the reasoning recorded. Maintain patch, currency and configuration compliance; remediate vulnerabilities and drift. Implement and maintain security and information governance controls in the collaboration estate: sensitivity labels, DLP, retention, external sharing controls, app consent and Conditional Access. Produce the evidence that audits require - configuration baselines, change records, access reviews - generated automatically wherever possible. Build to regulated-environment requirements where applicable, including GxP-validated systems and the qualification and change control they demand. Work daily with the Product Owner on refinement and estimation, and with the Architect on design; give honest estimates and flag risk early. Produce operational documentation, runbooks and knowledge articles good enough that the service desk can use them and the next engineer can pick the work up. Support and coach the service desk and second-line teams; reduce escalation volume by transferring capability, not by absorbing it. Mentor junior engineers and contribute to engineering standards and code review within the squad. 
 
 Education and Professional Qualifications 
 Bachelors degree in Computer Science, Engineering or a related discipline, or equivalent demonstrable professional experience. Strong practical experience is an acceptable substitute for formal qualification. Relevant certifications desirable (e.g., Microsoft 365 Certified: Administrator Expert, Teams Administrator Associate, Identity and Access Administrator Associate, Information Protection and Compliance Administrator, Power Platform Solution Architect, Azure Administrator, ITIL v4 Foundation). 
 
 Area of Specialisation 
 Hands-on Microsoft 365 platform engineering across the core collaboration workloads - Exchange Online, SharePoint Online / OneDrive and Microsoft Teams - at 50,000-user scale. Configuration-as-code for tenant settings - Git, CI/CD pipelines, automated validation and staged ring-based rollout - plus advanced PowerShell and Microsoft Graph automation. Microsoft Purview implementation - sensitivity labels, DLP, retention - and the practical behaviour of external sharing, Conditional Access and app consent controls once real users meet them. Complex collaboration-platform troubleshooting across client, identity, network and service layers, with root-cause elimination rather than ticket closure. 
 
 Experience Required 
 15 years overall and 10+ years in IT engineering or platform operations, including 5+ years working hands-on with Microsoft 365 in a production enterprise environment. Experience supporting or engineering a tenant of 5,000+ users; comfortable with the difference between a small tenant and a large one. Demonstrable hands-on capability across at least two of Exchange Online, SharePoint Online/OneDrive, or Microsoft Teams - at a level that includes troubleshooting, not only configuration. Working PowerShell proficiency with real examples of automation delivered into production, plus practical experience calling the Microsoft Graph API. Familiarity with Git and pull-request-based working; willingness to work configuration-as-code if not already doing so. Experience operating in an ITIL-aligned change and incident process, including production change ownership. Experience delivering within a Scrum or Kanban squad, including refinement, estimation and sprint commitment. Willingness to participate in an on-call rotation for major incidents. Fluent English, written and spoken; able to explain a technical issue to a non-technical colleague. 
 
 Desirable 
 Experience in a regulated industry - pharmaceutical, life sciences, biotech, financial services or healthcare - including GxP/CSV/CSA and validated-system change control. Migration delivery at scale - on-premises Exchange or SharePoint to cloud, file share to OneDrive/SharePoint, tenant-to-tenant, or third-party platform (Slack, Zoom, Google Workspace, Box) consolidation. Teams Phone / voice

The Senior SRE / Platform Engineer acts as a platform owner, enabling application teams through standardized infrastructure, GitOps workflows, policy enforcement, and observability. The position requires deep hands-on expertise across Kubernetes, AWS infrastructure, security tooling, and SRE operational practices. 
 Role & responsibilities

This role delivers secure, scalable, high-performance APIs and full-stack services while enabling AI-native consumption patterns across the enterprise.

Evaluate emerging patterns (event-driven integration, AI agent frameworks, low-code automation) to shape the platform roadmap. 
 
 Experience 
 8+ years of software engineering experience, with 5+ years in API/full-stack/backend development across multiple languages and clouds. 2+ years in a senior/lead/architect capacity owning API and platform designs for complex, enterprise-scale systems. 1+ years in an FDE role, working directly with internal customers. 
 
 Technical Skills - API, Fullstack Backend 
 Deep API expertise across REST, including contract-first design (OpenAPI/Swagger) and robust error handling. Strong backend and full-stack skills in Node.js / Java / Python / Go, plus platform-agnostic experience across cloud and iPaaS (MuleSoft, Workato, Boomi). Cloud-native development on AWS, Azure, or GCP, including serverless, Kubernetes, and infrastructure as code. Strong data skills - SQL and NoSQL database design, plus integration data formats (JSON, XML, CSV). Secure API design using OAuth 2.0/OIDC, mTLS, and secrets management, with solid CI/CD and Git-based workflows. SaaS integration experience with platforms such as NetSuite, Workday, Salesforce, or Snowflake. API Gateway expertise with platforms such as Kong / Apigee / AWS API Gateway / Azure APIM / MuleSoft API Gateway for routing, rate limiting, and policy enforcement. Working knowledge of AI/LLM frameworks (OpenAI, Anthropic, LangChain) and vector databases, and how they integrate with enterprise APIs. Understanding of AI-specific NFRs - latency, cost, rate limiting, and safety/guardrails. Practical experience with AI coding assistants (e.g., GitHub Copilot, Cursor, Claude Code) for AI assisted platform and infrastructure development. 
 
 Soft Skills

description:
Role & responsibilities 
 DevOps Engineer Azure, Automation, Splunk & Dynatrace
 Role Overview 
We are seeking a hands-on DevOps Engineer with strong experience in CI/CD, Azure infrastructure, automation, and containerized environments, complemented by administrative knowledge of Splunk and Dynatrace.
The role will focus on automating deployments, infrastructure, and observability setupensuring applications and services can be quickly onboarded, validated, and ready for production monitoring.
 Key Responsibilities 
1. CI/CD & Release Automation
Design and maintain pipelines using Jenkins, GitHub Actions, Azure DevOps, or equivalent tools. Automate builds, testing, deployments, and post-deployment validation, incorporating approval controls, rollback mechanisms, and secure release practices.
2. Azure Infrastructure & Infrastructure as Code
Provision and manage Azure services, including AKS, App Services, Azure Functions, networking, and storage. Use Terraform, Bicep, or equivalent tools to automate provisioning, standardize configurations, and improve scalability and cost efficiency.
3. Containerization & Kubernetes
Build and maintain Docker images and Kubernetes deployment configurations. Manage AKS workloads, scaling, resource allocation, and health checks; troubleshoot container, connectivity, and deployment issues.
4. Automation & Security
Develop reusable scripts using Python, PowerShell, or Bash to reduce manual effort across infrastructure, deployments, and operational workflows. Automate configuration management and integrate security scanning, secrets management, and access controls into delivery processes.
5. Splunk & Dynatrace Administration, Automation & Production Readiness
Automate platform setup, agent/forwarder deployment, configuration, and application onboarding to accelerate production-monitoring readiness. Support access management, platform health, and troubleshooting. Integrate reusable automation and readiness checks into CI/CD pipelines to validate log ingestion, telemetry collection, and monitoring coverage before go-live.
6. SRE & Production Reliability
Apply SRE principles, including SLIs, SLOs, error budgets, incident management, and post-incident reviews. Partner with SRE L2/L3 teams to resolve production issues, reduce MTTR, and automate recurring operational and recovery activities.
7. Collaboration & Enablement 
Provide reusable automation templates, operational runbooks, and engineering standards. Enable self-service provisioning and monitoring onboarding, integrate workflows with ServiceNow or Jira, and guide teams on deployment and operational readiness. 
 Required Qualifications 
5+ years of hands-on DevOps or platform engineering experience, including CI/CD ownership, infrastructure automation, and production troubleshooting.
Strong experience with Jenkins, GitHub Actions, Azure DevOps, or equivalent tools, along with Git-based workflows.
Hands-on expertise in Microsoft Azure, Infrastructure as Code, Docker, Kubernetes/AKS, and Linux.
Strong scripting skills in Python, PowerShell, or Bash, including API-based automation and tool integration.
Working administrative knowledge of both Splunk and Dynatrace, including access management, forwarder/agent configuration, data onboarding, platform health, and troubleshooting.
Ability to automate monitoring setup, streamline application onboarding, and validate production-monitoring readiness.
Understanding of SRE fundamentals, with strong analytical, communication, and cross-functional collaboration skills.
 Preferred Qualifications 
Experience supporting retail/e-commerce platforms, microservices, and distributed systems. Familiarity with Helm, GitOps/Argo CD, Prometheus, and Grafana.
Certifications in Azure, Kubernetes, Terraform, Splunk, or Dynatrace are good to have, but not mandatory.
Success Measures
Reduced time to onboard applications into production monitoring; increased automation and self-service adoption; validated monitoring coverage before go-live; fewer manual configuration errors; and improved deployment reliability and incident resolution time.

description:

It is the largest managed health care company in the Blue Cross Blue Shield (BCBS) Association serving more than 112 million individuals across 14 states. A regular in Fortune 500 list, Elevance Health ranked 18 in 2026. Gail Boudreaux , President and CEO of Elevance Health has been a consistent name in the Fortune list of most powerful women and currently holds 81st rank on this list. ABOUT CARELON GLOBAL SOLUTIONS Carelon Global Solutions (CGS) is a healthcare solutions company simplifying complex operational processes to improve the health of the healthcare system. Previously known as Legato Health Technologies, Carelon Global Solutions (hereinafter, CGS) underwent a name change and joined the Carelon family of brands in January 2023, as a fully owned subsidiary of Elevance Health (Previously Anthem Inc.). CGS brings together a global team of like-minded innovators who manage and optimize operational processes for health plans as well as providers. Our brightest minds housed across our global headquarters in Indianapolis as well as Bengaluru, Hyderabad and Gurugram in India, Manila in the Philippines, and San Juan in Puerto Rico bring with them innovative capabilities and an unmatched depth of experience. This global team uniquely positions CGS to enable scalable, next-generation platforms and specialized digital tools that make healthcare operations more practical, effective, and efficient. OUR MISSION & VALUES Our Mission: Improving Lives and Communities. Simplifying Healthcare. Expecting More.
 Our Values: Leadership | Community | Integrity | Agility | Diversity JOB PURPOSE Carelon Global Solutions India is seeking a Senior Manager Architecture to lead architecture and end-to-end implementation of enterprise pharmacy management capabilities for CarelonRx. The role owns technical vision, solution architecture, engineering execution, implementation readiness, and platform outcomes across complex, multi-system pharmacy transformation programs. The position is intentionally weighted toward architecture, engineering, AI-enabled Spec-Driven Development, and large-scale implementation leadership. Delivery administration is a supporting responsibility, not the primary mandate. The leader will combine strong software engineering depth with practical pharmacy and PBM domain knowledge to translate business capabilities into secure, scalable, resilient, and operable platforms. JOB RESPONSIBILITY Enterprise Pharmacy Architecture Define and govern target-state solution architecture for end-to-end pharmacy management systems, aligned with enterprise architecture, security, data, privacy, resiliency, and regulatory guardrails. Create capability maps, domain boundaries, reference architectures, reusable patterns, integration standards, and modernization roadmaps across the pharmacy ecosystem. Lead architecture decisions for microservices, APIs, event streaming, workflow orchestration, data platforms, cloud-native services, observability, and interoperability with legacy platforms. Own architecture reviews, trade-off decisions, non-functional requirements, technical debt strategy, and design assurance from concept through production adoption. End-To-End Pharmacy Platform Implementation Lead implementation across relevant pharmacy and PBM capabilities such as benefit configuration, formulary, eligibility, claims adjudication, pricing, prior authorization, pharmacy networks, specialty pharmacy, clinical programs, rebates, member and provider experiences, and operational reporting. Translate business journeys and pharmacy operating models into domain-aligned services, data contracts, interfaces, implementation increments, migration plans, and measurable acceptance criteria. Own the technical implementation lifecycle covering discovery, architecture, engineering, integration, data conversion, testing strategy, cutover, production readiness, stabilization, and benefits realization. Manage cross-platform dependencies and ensure that application, data, infrastructure, security, operations, and vendor workstreams converge into one implementable solution. Drive phased rollout, coexistence, migration, and decommissioning strategies that protect member, client, pharmacy, and operational continuity. AI-Enabled Spec-Driven Development (SDD) Establish an AI-first Spec-Driven Development approach in which approved business, architecture, interface, security, testing, and operational specifications become the governed source for implementation. Enable engineering agents and copilots to accelerate design elaboration, code generation, test creation, documentation, code review, traceability, and impact analysis, with human review and approval at critical control points. Define reusable SDD templates, prompt and context standards, repository conventions, quality gates, evaluation criteria, and responsible AI controls for enterprise adoption. Measure SDD outcomes using baselines and agreed targets for engineering cycle time, specification-to-code traceability, automated test coverage, escaped defects, rework, deployment frequency, and productivity improvement. Ensure AI-generated artifacts meet enterprise standards for security, privacy, intellectual property, explainability, maintainability, and auditability. Engineering Excellence And Hands-On Technical Leadership Provide credible, hands-on technical leadership through design reviews, code and API reviews, proof-of-concept direction, critical problem solving, performance analysis, and production diagnostics. Guide teams on software design principles, domain-driven design, secure coding, automated testing, DevSecOps, CI/CD, infrastructure as code, reliability engineering, and cloud cost optimization. Define engineering scorecards and quality gates covering code health, architecture compliance, security vulnerabilities, reliability, performance, recoverability, maintainability, and operational readiness. Champion platform engineering, reusable services, developer experience, automated environments, and self-service capabilities that reduce implementation friction at scale. Large-Scale Implementation Leadership Lead multiple engineering teams and technical workstreams across product, architecture, software engineering, data, quality engineering, cloud, security, operations, and partner organizations. Create an integrated technical implementation plan that connects architecture runway, dependency sequencing, environment readiness, test strategy, migration, cutover, and operational acceptance. Act as the senior technical decision-maker for complex implementation risks, cross-team conflicts, architecture exceptions, integration failures, and production-readiness gaps. Provide transparent executive-level reporting on architecture health, implementation progress, critical dependencies, risk exposure, quality, readiness, and realized business outcomes. Build governance that is lightweight but effective, emphasizing decision velocity, measurable technical outcomes, and removal of systemic blockers rather than delivery administration. Pharmacy Domain And Stakeholder Partnership Apply working knowledge of the prescription lifecycle, PBM operations, payer and pharmacy interactions, clinical and utilization management, drug data, pricing, formulary, claims, and applicable industry transactions and regulations. Partner with pharmacy business leaders, product managers, enterprise architects, security, operations, compliance, and client teams to shape solutions that are technically sound and operationally adoptable. Convert domain policies, rules, and exceptions into explicit specifications, testable requirements, decision services, and traceable implementation controls. Challenge assumptions using outside-in engineering and pharmacy-platform practices while tailoring recommendations to CarelonRx business priorities and enterprise constraints. People And Capability Leadership Build, lead, and mentor engineering managers, solution architects, principal engineers, technical leads, developers, quality engineers, and platform specialists across distributed teams. Establish clear technical accountabilities, architecture ownership, engineering career paths, succession plans, and communities of practice for pharmacy engineering and AI SDD. Create a culture of engineering rigor, transparent decision-making, experimentation, learning, inclusion, and accountability for outcomes. Assess capability gaps and execute hiring, upskilling, partner augmentation, and workforce plans required for large-scale implementation. Delivery Governance As A Supporting Responsibility Partner with product and program leadership on planning, investment sequencing, release readiness, dependency management, and risk escalation. Use delivery metrics only as supporting indicators. Primary accountability remains architecture quality, end-to-end implementation integrity, engineering excellence, and business capability outcomes. Ensure commitments are realistic, technically grounded, and supported by clear specifications, measurable acceptance criteria, and production-readiness evidence. QUALIFICATION Bachelors degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Information Technology, or a related discipline; postgraduate qualification is preferred. Strong foundation in software engineering, enterprise solution architecture, systems integration, cloud engineering, data architecture, cybersecurity, and operational resilience. Demonstrated ability to communicate architecture and implementation choices to business executives, product leaders, engineers, risk partners, and external vendors. Ability to lead through ambiguity, make evidence-based trade-offs, and connect pharmacy business outcomes to technical architecture and implementation decisions. Working knowledge of Agile, product operating models, DevSecOps, secure SDLC, and modern engineering governance. EXPERIENCE 15+ years of progressive experience in software engineering, solution architecture, enterprise platforms, and technology implementation, including 5+ years leading engineering managers, architects, or large technical teams. Proven leadership of large-scale, multi-year enterprise implementations involving multiple applications, complex integrations, data migration, cloud platforms, distributed teams, and production cutover. Relevant healthcare, pharmacy, or PBM experience, with demonstrable understanding of end-to-end pharmacy capabilities and their technology implications. Demonstrated experience defining target architecture and taking complex platforms from architecture through implementation, production readiness, stabilization, and measurable adoption. Experience applying AI-assisted engineering, Spec-Driven Development, agentic workflows, or comparable automation across the SDLC with appropriate human oversight and governance. Experience managing strategic vendors and globally distributed teams while retaining internal ownership of architecture, engineering quality, and implementation outcomes. Experience modernizing legacy systems using APIs, microservices, event-driven patterns, cloud-native platforms, automated testing, DevSecOps, observability, and reliability practices. SKILLS AND COMPETENCIES Core Technical Competencies Enterprise and solution architecture; domain-driven design; capability modeling; microservices; API-first and event-driven architecture; integration and interoperability patterns. Java and/or .NET engineering ecosystems; REST and GraphQL APIs; event-streaming platforms; containers and Kubernetes; Azure and/or AWS; CI/CD; infrastructure as code; observability and SRE practices. Data architecture, master and reference data, transactional and analytical data patterns, data quality, lineage, privacy, and secure information exchange. Architecture fitness functions, performance engineering, resilience, disaster recovery, security-by-design, threat modeling, and production operability. Pharmacy And Healthcare Domain Competencies Prescription and pharmacy claims lifecycle; benefit configuration; formulary and utilization management; eligibility; pricing; pharmacy networks; specialty and mail pharmacy; clinical programs; rebates; member and provider journeys. Awareness of healthcare and pharmacy interoperability, transaction standards, regulatory obligations, data privacy, and audit requirements relevant to the assigned platform scope. AI and SDD Competencies Spec-Driven Development, AI-assisted software engineering, agent orchestration, retrieval and context patterns, prompt and evaluation practices, automated testing, traceability, and responsible AI governance. Ability to establish engineering baselines, controlled pilots, adoption guardrails, and measurable value realization for AI-enabled development. Leadership Competencies Strategic thinking, systems thinking, executive communication, architecture decision-making, technical talent development, vendor leadership, influencing without authority, and crisis leadership. Bias for simplification, measurable outcomes, engineering quality, operational accountability, and continuous improvement. Preferred Certifications Cloud architecture certification in Azure or AWS. AI, machine learning, responsible AI, or generative AI certification. Healthcare or pharmacy domain certification, where applicable. SAFe Agilist or equivalent product and Agile leadership certification. Indicative Success Measures Architecture: target-state adoption, design conformance, reuse, technical debt reduction, resilience, security, and platform scalability. Implementation: capability readiness, integration completeness, migration quality, cutover readiness, production stability, adoption, and business outcome realization. Engineering: cycle-time improvement, automation coverage, defect escape reduction, reliability, developer experience, and maintainability. AI SDD: specification coverage and traceability, governed AI adoption, reusable agent workflows, quality of generated artifacts, and validated productivity benefits. Organization: critical-skill coverage, leadership bench strength, team health, succession readiness, and growth of architecture and engineering capability. Delivery: predictable release support and governance compliance, intentionally weighted below architecture, implementation, engineering, and business outcomes. description:
Senior DevOps Engineer Linux / VMware / Terraform 
 Location : Bangalore
 Work Mode : 100% On-site

 Employment : Full-time 
 Role Overview We are looking for a highly experienced Senior DevOps Engineer with strong hands-on expertise in Linux infrastructure, VMware, Infrastructure as Code, automation, CI/CD, containers, and cloud technologies. 
 This is a highly hands-on role for someone who can independently design, automate, troubleshoot, and improve infrastructure rather than simply maintain existing systems. 
 You will work closely with our US-based engineering teams to modernize our infrastructure, expand automation, strengthen CI/CD processes, and move traditional infrastructure toward an Infrastructure-as-Code and DevOps-driven model. 
 Key Responsibilities Design and implement Infrastructure as Code using Terraform/Terragrunt and Ansible. Administer and troubleshoot Ubuntu Linux servers across VMware, colocated infrastructure, and cloud environments. Manage and improve VMware vSphere, ESXi, and vCenter environments. Build and maintain automation for provisioning, configuration, patching, backups, and infrastructure lifecycle management. Develop and enhance CI/CD pipelines using Jenkins and Bitbucket. Manage containerized workloads using Docker, Docker Compose, and Portainer. Support AWS infrastructure including EC2, RDS, S3, ECS Fargate, IAM, CloudWatch, VPN, and related services. Troubleshoot complex infrastructure, Linux, networking, application deployment, database, and performance issues. Support services including MySQL, Redis, Apache, Cloudflare, Active Directory, and Authentik. Implement security best practices including least-privilege access, secrets management, network segmentation, logging, and monitoring. Work with monitoring tools including Zabbix, ELK/Elastic Stack, Sentry, and CloudWatch. Collaborate directly with developers and infrastructure teams to improve deployment reliability and eliminate repetitive manual work. Participate in infrastructure incident response and on-call support when required. Required Skills 8+ years of hands-on experience in Linux / DevOps / Infrastructure Engineering Strong Linux administration and troubleshooting experience Strong VMware vSphere / ESXi / vCenter administration Strong hands-on experience with Terraform Experience with Ansible Strong understanding of Infrastructure as Code Experience building and troubleshooting CI/CD pipelines Hands-on experience with Jenkins Strong Docker and containerization knowledge AWS infrastructure experience Strong networking fundamentals including TCP/IP, DNS, routing, VPN, firewall, and reverse proxy concepts Experience with Bash or other infrastructure scripting Strong troubleshooting and root-cause-analysis skills Ability to work independently without requiring constant supervision 
 Preferred Skills Experience with some of the following will be advantageous: Terragrunt, Bitbucket, MySQL, Redis, Percona XtraBackup, Zabbix, ELK, Elastic Agent, Sentry, CloudWatch, Cloudflare, Apache, Active Directory, Authentik, Laravel/PHP environments, and Vue.js application environments. Experience supporting HIPAA-regulated or other security/compliance-sensitive environments is also preferred. 
 Important Work Requirements This position is 100% on-site in Bangalore and works closely with US-based engineering teams during US business hours / India night shift. Please apply only if you are genuinely comfortable working this schedule on a long-term basis. 
 We are looking for someone who enjoys solving difficult infrastructure problems, taking ownership, automating repetitive work, and improving systems rather than waiting for detailed instructions.

Location: Bangalore/Pune

Education Qualification: Bachelors degree in computer science or related field or higher with minimum 12 years of relevant experience.

We are seeking an experienced Technical Manager - Delivery to lead engineering delivery for enterprise AI solutions and reusable AI platform capabilities. The role combines strong technical leadership with delivery and people management. The candidate will guide developers, AI engineers, QA and DevOps engineers; challenge architecture and design decisions; drive engineering quality, security, scalability and production readiness; and ensure predictable delivery of business outcomes.

The ideal candidate should have a strong application engineering foundation in Java and/or Python, APIs, microservices and cloud-native platforms, together with practical experience delivering Generative AI solutions using LLMs, RAG and agentic AI patterns. The role does not require an AI research background; the emphasis is enterprise AI application engineering and technical delivery leadership. 

 Your future duties and responsibilities: 
 Technical & Delivery Leadership
- Lead end-to-end technical delivery of enterprise AI solutions, GenAI applications and reusable AI platform capabilities from design through production.
- Provide technical direction and review solution architecture, detailed design, APIs, integration patterns, code quality, performance, scalability and security.
- Guide implementation of LLM-based solutions including RAG, agentic workflows, tool calling, orchestration, prompt engineering and enterprise integrations.
- Own sprint and release planning, estimation, resource allocation, technical dependencies, risks, quality and delivery commitments.
- Drive production readiness, incident resolution, root-cause analysis, performance optimization and continuous improvement of AI services and platforms.
Team Engagement & People Leadership
- Lead, mentor and engage cross-functional teams comprising AI/application developers, technical leads, QA and DevOps engineers.
- Build a strong engineering culture focused on collaboration, ownership, innovation, knowledge sharing and continuous improvement.
- Conduct regular team connect sessions, 1:1s and feedback discussions; identify engagement risks, impediments and actions to improve team effectiveness.
- Drive hiring, onboarding, career development, performance management, succession planning and targeted upskilling in AI engineering and modern development practices.
- Identify skill gaps and create technical learning plans, communities of practice and opportunities for team members to contribute to reusable AI assets.
Operations & Engineering Management
- Own delivery operations for the technical organization, with accountability for revenue, gross margin, net margin, cost, utilization and overall delivery health.
- Track actuals versus plan for revenue, gross margin and net margin; identify variances early and drive corrective actions with delivery and leadership teams.
- Prepare revenue and resource forecasts, including capacity planning, demand pipeline, ramp-up/ramp-down plans, hiring needs and allocation of technical resources across engagements.
- Monitor team utilization and bench levels, balancing billable delivery, platform investments, production support, technical debt and capability development.
- Drive productivity and engineering efficiency through automation, AI-enabled development, reuse of platform capabilities and continuous improvement initiatives.
- Establish and review operational KPIs covering revenue attainment, margin performance, utilization, productivity, delivery predictability, quality, automation, incidents and customer commitments.
- Lead operational governance including monthly/quarterly business reviews, financial reviews, resource reviews, risk and dependency reviews, and action tracking.
- Partner with account, finance, sales and delivery leadership on forecasting, financial planning, staffing decisions, pricing inputs and opportunities to improve delivery economics.
AI Engineering & Quality
- Establish AI quality and reliability practices covering evaluation, grounding, hallucination reduction, guardrails, latency, cost, monitoring and human-in-the-loop controls where appropriate.
- Promote AI-enabled software development practices using coding assistants/agents for development, testing, code review and engineering productivity, with appropriate governance.
Stakeholder & Cross-functional Collaboration
- Partner with Product Owners, Business Analysts, Architects and business stakeholders to translate business problems into scalable technical solutions.
- Communicate technical risks, trade-offs, delivery status and operational performance clearly to leadership and non-technical stakeholders. 

 Required qualifications to be successful in this role: 
 Must to Have Skills:
12+ years of software engineering experience with significant technical leadership and delivery management responsibility.
- Recent practical experience delivering enterprise GenAI/AI applications or platforms.
- Strong understanding of LLM application patterns: prompt engineering, RAG, embeddings, vector search/vector databases and model evaluation.
- Understanding of agentic AI concepts including agents, tool/function calling, workflow orchestration, state/memory and human-in-the-loop patterns.
- Strong backend engineering experience in Java/Spring Boot and/or Python/FastAPI, with REST APIs, microservices and distributed application architecture.
- Experience designing or managing reusable platform services and enterprise integrations rather than only standalone AI proofs of concept.
- Cloud-native engineering experience on Azure, AWS or GCP, with Docker and Kubernetes/OpenShift.
- Strong DevOps engineering knowledge including Git, CI/CD, automated testing, release management and environment management.
- Understanding of LLMOps/MLOps practices including prompt/model configuration versioning, evaluation, monitoring, observability and controlled deployment.
- Strong understanding of enterprise security including authentication/authorization, secrets management, data privacy, secure API integration and responsible AI controls.
- Proven experience managing developers, QA and DevOps engineers and driving engineering standards, technical reviews and production readiness.
- Strong Agile delivery, estimation, planning, risk/dependency management and stakeholder communication skills.
- Demonstrated experience using or enabling AI-assisted development tools responsibly across the software development lifecycle.

 Nice-to-Have / Added Advantages

 We are looking for a Cloud Platform Engineer who can seamlessly manage operations and infrastructure provisioning within a complex, growing multi-cloud environment. Your primary responsibility will be building, scaling, and troubleshooting cloud infrastructure using modern GitOps practices. You will serve as a core operator for our platform, fulfilling infrastructure requests while actively writing automation to eliminate manual toil and enhance developer velocity. Furthermore, you will help lay the operational groundwork for emerging technologies, including hosting and integrating AI inferencing workloads. We need a hands-on builder with strong programming fundamentals and a deep understanding of cloud operations. This position is an individual contributor role reporting to the Director, Developer Platform Engineering. 
 
 Responsibilities 
 Provision, modify, and manage cloud infrastructure across our multi-cloud environment (heavily focused on AWS) using Terraform Build and maintain CI/CD pipelines and GitOps workflows using GitHub Actions (or equivalent tooling) Manage and operate core platform technologies including EKS (Kubernetes), Argo CD Write automation scripts and CLI tooling using Python or Go to eliminate manual operational toil and streamline developer access Support the deployment and configuration of infrastructure required for AI inferencing and internal AI tooling Troubleshoot complex platform issues ranging from Kubernetes networking to cloud IAM permissions and pipeline bottlenecks Own the design, development, and operation of a Backstage-based Developer Portal that enables citizen builders to build, deploy, and manage applications with minimal platform expertise 
 
 Job Designation 
 Hybrid: Employee divides their time between in-office and remote work. Access to an office location is required. (Frequency: Minimum 2 days per week; may vary by team but will be weekly in-office expectation) Positions at Docusign are assigned a job designation of either In Office, Hybrid or Remote and are specific to the role/job. Preferred job designations are not guaranteed when changing positions within Docusign. Docusign reserves the right to change a positions job designation depending on business needs and as permitted by local law. 
 
 What you bring 
 Basic A Computer Science degree or equivalent practical experience 8+ years of hands-on experience in Cloud Engineering or Platform Engineering roles Deep expertise in AWS core services, networking, and IAM architectures Advanced proficiency in Terraform (module creation, state management) and GitOps principles Strong hands-on experience configuring and maintaining GitHub Actions (or similar CI/CD platforms) Production experience operating Kubernetes (EKS) and deployment tools like Argo CD Experience with secrets management (e.g., HashiCorp Vault), modern observability stacks (Datadog, Prometheus, Grafana) and Artifact management (JFrog) Preferred Experience operating within a multi-cloud ecosystem (AWS, Azure, GCP, etc.) Solid programming capability in Python or Go for infrastructure automation and tooling Strong expertise in building modern web applications and deploying, scaling, and managing them in cloud environments
